title_en: Be sure the sentence has a subject and a verb
title_id: Pastikan kalimat punya subject dan verb
summary_id: Di soal Structure TOEFL, kesalahan paling umum adalah subject hilang, verb hilang, atau ada subject/verb tambahan yang tidak perlu.
summary_en: On TOEFL Structure, the most common errors are a missing subject, a missing verb, or an extra subject/verb.

formula.label: Inti aturan
formula.en: SUBJECT + VERB (+ …)
formula.id: Setiap kalimat minimal: SUBJECT + VERB

formula.label: Cek cepat
formula.en:
1) Who/What is the sentence about? → SUBJECT
2) What happens / is true? → VERB
formula.id:
1) Tentang siapa/apa? → SUBJECT
2) Apa yang terjadi / keadaannya? → VERB

formula.label: Larangan
formula.en: ❌ No subject  ·  ❌ No verb  ·  ❌ Double subject (e.g. The boy he is…)
formula.id: ❌ Tanpa subject  ·  ❌ Tanpa verb  ·  ❌ Subject dobel (The boy he is…)

rules.body_id: Subject = pelaku / topik kalimat (noun, pronoun, atau noun phrase). Tanpa subject, kalimat tidak lengkap.
rules.body_en: The subject is who or what the sentence is about. Without it, the sentence is incomplete.

rules.title_en: 2. There must be a finite verb
rules.body_id: Verb harus bentuk lengkap (is/are/was, works, has gone, will be…). Participle saja (going, needed) sering belum cukup tanpa be/aux.
rules.body_en: You need a full verb form. A participle alone (going, needed) is often not enough without be/an auxiliary.

rules.title_en: 3. Do not add an extra subject
rules.body_id: Jika sudah ada The boy, jangan tambah he. Pola salah: The boy he is going…
rules.body_en: If the sentence already has The boy, do not add he. Wrong: The boy he is going…

rules.body_id: Subject singular → verb singular (traffic was…). Subject plural → verb plural (cars were…). Pilih subject yang cocok dengan verb yang sudah ada.
rules.body_en: Singular subject → singular verb; plural → plural. Pick a subject that agrees with the given verb.

examples.stem: _____ was backed up for miles on the freeway.
examples.why_en: There is a verb (was) but no subject. Traffic is a singular subject that agrees with was. Yesterday / In the morning are not subjects. Cars is plural, so it does not agree with was.
examples.why_id: Sudah ada verb was, tapi belum ada subject. Traffic (singular) cocok dengan was. Yesterday / In the morning bukan subject. Cars plural → tidak cocok dengan was.

examples.stem: Engineers _____ for work on the new space program.
examples.why_en: The sentence has a subject (Engineers) but no verb. Are needed is the verb phrase that completes the sentence. The other options are not verbs.
examples.why_id: Sudah ada subject Engineers, tapi belum ada verb. Are needed melengkapi kalimat. Opsi lain bukan verb.

examples.stem: The boy _____ going to the movies with a friend.
examples.why_en: Subject boy already exists; going needs a form of be. Will be + going is complete. He is / he always was add an extra subject he. Is relaxing adds an unnecessary extra verb idea beside going.
examples.why_id: Subject boy sudah ada; going butuh be. Will be + going lengkap. He is / he always was menambah subject he. Is relaxing menambah verb yang tidak perlu di samping going.

checklist_id: Tandai subject (siapa/apa).
Tandai verb finite (kata kerja utama).
Cek: apakah subject hilang?
Cek: apakah verb hilang?
Cek: ada subject/verb ekstra?
Cek agreement (singular/plural).
checklist_en: Mark the subject (who/what).
Mark the finite verb.
Missing subject?
Missing verb?
Extra subject or verb?
Agreement (singular/plural)?
remember_id: Kalimat Inggris minimal: **SUBJECT + VERB**. Hilang salah satu → salah. Dobel subject/verb → salah.
remember_en: An English sentence needs at least **SUBJECT + VERB**. Missing either is wrong. An extra subject/verb is also wrong.

title_en: Be careful of objects of prepositions
summary_id: Object of preposition (noun/pronoun/gerund setelah in, of, with, by, dll.) sering dikira subject. Kata itu BUKAN subject — cari subject yang sesungguhnya.
summary_en: An object of a preposition (noun/pronoun/gerund after in, of, with, by, etc.) is often mistaken for the subject. It is NOT the subject — find the real subject.

formula.label: Pola prepositional phrase
formula.en:
PREPOSITION + OBJECT
(with + friend)  (after + exams)  (by + boat)
formula.id:
PREPOSITION + OBJECT
(with + friend)  (after + exams)  (by + boat)

formula.label: Aturan inti
formula.en:
Object of a preposition ≠ SUBJECT
One noun cannot be subject and object at the same time.
formula.id:
Object of preposition ≠ SUBJECT
Satu noun tidak bisa jadi subject dan object sekaligus.

formula.label: Cek cepat
formula.en:
1) Circle prepositions (in, on, of, to, by, with…)
2) Mark the noun after them = OBJECT (not subject)
3) Find the real SUBJECT + VERB outside the phrase
formula.id:
1) Lingkari preposition (in, on, of, to, by, with…)
2) Noun setelahnya = OBJECT (bukan subject)
3) Cari SUBJECT + VERB di luar frase itu

rules.title_en: 1. What is an object of a preposition?
rules.body_id: Noun, pronoun, gerund, atau noun clause yang mengikuti preposition (in, at, of, to, by, behind, on, with, from, for, …) membentuk prepositional phrase.
rules.body_en: A noun, pronoun, gerund, or noun clause after a preposition (in, at, of, to, by, behind, on, with, from, for, …) forms a prepositional phrase.

rules.body_id: After his exams → exams = object of after. By boat → boat = object of by. With his friend → friend = object of with.
rules.body_en: After his exams → exams = object of after. By boat → boat = object of by. With his friend → friend = object of with.

rules.title_en: 3. Do not mistake it for the subject
rules.body_id: Di soal Structure, object of preposition sering panjang dan dekat verb, jadi mudah dikira subject. Ingat: jika sudah jadi object, tidak bisa jadi subject di clause yang sama.
rules.body_en: In Structure items, the object of a preposition can look like the subject. Remember: if a word is an object of a preposition, it is not the subject.

rules.title_id: 4. Subject–verb agreement tetap mengikuti subject asli
rules.body_id: The results of the experiment were… → subject = results (plural), bukan experiment. The cost of materials has risen… → subject = cost (singular).
rules.body_en: The results of the experiment were… → subject = results (plural), not experiment. The cost of materials has risen… → subject = cost (singular).

examples.stem: With his friend _____ found the movie theater.
examples.why_en: found is the verb; there is no subject yet. friend is the object of with, so it cannot be the subject. Answer (B) he supplies the subject.
examples.why_id: found = verb; subject belum ada. friend = object of with, jadi bukan subject. Jawaban (B) he mengisi subject.

examples.stem: The results of the multi-site experiment _____ published last month.
examples.why_en: Subject = results (plural), not experiment (object of of). Plural subject → were.
examples.why_id: Subject = results (plural), bukan experiment (object of of). Subject plural → were.

examples.stem: Each of the participating laboratories _____ a full replication package.
examples.why_en: Each is singular; of the laboratories is only a prepositional phrase. Singular → submits.
examples.why_id: Each singular; of the laboratories hanya prepositional phrase. Singular → submits.

checklist_id: Lingkari semua preposition (of, in, with, by, from…).
Tandai object setelah preposition — itu BUKAN subject.
Cari subject di luar prepositional phrase.
Cocokkan verb dengan subject asli (bukan dengan object of preposition).
Cek singular/plural: one/each/none vs a number of / results / effects.
checklist_en: Circle every preposition (of, in, with, by, from…).
Mark the object after it — that is NOT the subject.
Find the real subject outside the prepositional phrase.
Make the verb agree with the real subject (not the object of the preposition).
Check singular/plural: one/each/none vs a number of / results / effects.
remember_id: Preposition + object. **Object of preposition ≠ subject.** Agreement mengikuti subject yang sebenarnya.
remember_en: Preposition + object. **Object of a preposition ≠ subject.** Agreement follows the real subject.

summary_id: Appositive = noun yang menjelaskan noun lain (biasanya di antara koma). Appositive bukan subject. Jangan sampai tertukar dengan subject kalimat.
summary_en: An appositive is a noun that renames another noun (usually set off by commas). An appositive is not the subject — do not confuse the two.

formula.label: Pola A — appositive setelah subject
formula.en:
S , APP , V …
Tom, a really good mechanic, is fixing the car.
formula.id:
S , APP , V …
Tom, a really good mechanic, is fixing the car.

formula.label: Pola B — appositive di depan
formula.en:
APP , S V …
A really good mechanic, Tom is fixing the car.
formula.id:
APP , S V …
A really good mechanic, Tom is fixing the car.

formula.label: Tes cepat
formula.en:
Remove the phrase between commas.
If the sentence still works → that phrase is likely an appositive (not the subject).
formula.id:
Hapus frase di antara koma.
Kalimat masih masuk akal → itu kemungkinan besar appositive (bukan subject).

rules.body_id: Noun (atau noun phrase) yang datang sebelum/sesudah noun lain dan punya makna yang sama. Contoh: Sally, the best student in the class, got an A. Sally = the best student.
rules.body_en: A noun (or noun phrase) before or after another noun with the same meaning. Example: Sally, the best student in the class, got an A. Sally = the best student.

rules.body_id: Koma menandai appositive. Jika ada koma mengapit sebuah noun phrase, cek apakah itu hanya menjelaskan subject — bukan subject itu sendiri.
rules.body_en: Commas often mark the appositive. If commas surround a noun phrase, check whether it only renames the subject — it is not the subject itself.

rules.title_en: 3. An appositive is not the subject
rules.body_id: Subject tetap noun utama di luar appositive. Kalimat tetap butuh subject + verb yang lengkap; appositive tidak menggantikan subject.
rules.body_en: The subject is the main noun outside the appositive. The sentence still needs a full subject + verb; the appositive does not replace the subject.

rules.title_en: 4. An appositive does not need its own verb
rules.body_id: Jangan pilih opsi yang menyisipkan is/was ke dalam appositive. An excellent basketball player (benar) vs An excellent basketball player is (salah sebagai appositive).
rules.body_en: Do not choose options that insert is/was into the appositive. An excellent basketball player (correct) vs An excellent basketball player is (wrong as an appositive).

examples.stem: _____ George, is attending the lecture.
examples.why_en: Commas show that George is an appositive, not the subject. The sentence still needs a subject → My friend. (A)–(C) cannot be subjects.
examples.why_id: Koma menunjukkan George adalah appositive, bukan subject. Kalimat masih butuh subject → My friend. (A)–(C) tidak bisa jadi subject.

examples.stem: _____ Sarah rarely misses her basketball shots.
options: Sarah is an excellent basketball player
examples.why_en: Sarah is the subject and misses is the verb (no comma between them). Put an appositive for Sarah: An excellent basketball player. (B)(C) add an extra verb is. (D) play is not the same as Sarah.
examples.why_id: Sarah = subject, misses = verb (tanpa koma di antaranya). Isi appositive untuk Sarah: An excellent basketball player. (B)(C) menambah verb is. (D) play bukan sama dengan Sarah.

examples.stem: The tetracyclines, _____ antibiotics, are used to treat infections.
examples.why_en: Between commas you need a noun phrase appositive: a family of antibiotics. Not a second main verb (are / is).
examples.why_id: Di antara koma butuh noun phrase appositive: a family of antibiotics. Bukan verb utama kedua (are / is).

checklist_id: Cari koma yang mengapit noun phrase.
Tandai appositive — itu menjelaskan noun, bukan subject.
Hapus sementara appositive; sisa kalimat harus tetap punya subject + verb.
Pastikan appositive tidak membawa verb finite sendiri (is/was/are).
Subject–verb agreement mengikuti subject utama, bukan isi appositive.
checklist_en: Find commas around a noun phrase.
Mark the appositive — it renames a noun; it is not the subject.
Temporarily remove the appositive; the rest must still have subject + verb.
Make sure the appositive does not carry its own finite verb (is/was/are).
Agreement follows the main subject, not the appositive phrase.
remember_id: Appositive = noun penjelas (sering di antara koma). **Appositive ≠ subject.** Kalimat tetap butuh subject + verb di luar appositive.
remember_en: An appositive is a renaming noun (often between commas). **Appositive ≠ subject.** The sentence still needs subject + verb outside the appositive.

summary_id: Present participle (-ing) bisa jadi bagian verb (dengan be) atau adjective (tanpa be). Jangan sampai -ing dikira verb utama padahal hanya modifier.
summary_en: A present participle (-ing) can be part of the verb (with be) or an adjective (without be). Do not treat -ing as the main verb when it is only a modifier.

formula.label: Sebagai bagian VERB
formula.en:
be + V-ing  →  verb phrase
The man is talking to his friend.
formula.id:
be + V-ing  →  frasa verb
The man is talking to his friend.

formula.label: Sebagai ADJECTIVE
formula.en:
Noun + V-ing …  (no be before it)
The man talking to his friend has a beard.
→ talking = adjective; main verb = has
formula.id:
Noun + V-ing …  (tanpa be di depannya)
The man talking to his friend has a beard.
→ talking = adjective; verb utama = has

formula.label: Cek cepat
formula.en:
Is there a form of be right before -ing?
YES → part of the verb
NO  → usually adjective (look for another finite verb)
formula.id:
Ada be tepat sebelum -ing?
YA  → bagian verb
TIDAK → biasanya adjective (cari finite verb lain)

rules.body_id: Bentuk -ing dari verb (talking, playing, standing). Di Structure TOEFL, bisa membingungkan karena kadang verb, kadang adjective.
rules.body_en: The -ing form of a verb (talking, playing, standing). On TOEFL Structure it can be confusing because it may be part of the verb or an adjective.

rules.title_en: 2. With be = part of the verb
rules.body_id: The boy is standing in the corner. → is standing = verb lengkap. is = be, standing = present participle.
rules.body_en: The boy is standing in the corner. → is standing = full verb phrase. is = be, standing = present participle.

rules.body_id: The boy standing in the corner was naughty. → standing menjelaskan boy; verb utama = was. Jangan menambah is/was lagi di tempat yang salah.
rules.body_en: The boy standing in the corner was naughty. → standing modifies boy; main verb = was. Do not insert another is/was incorrectly.

rules.body_id: Jika kalimat sudah punya is/has/was di tempat lain, -ing di tengah sering hanya reduced relative (adjective), bukan verb yang butuh dilengkapi.
rules.body_en: If the sentence already has is/has/was elsewhere, a mid-sentence -ing is often only a reduced relative (adjective), not a verb that still needs completing.

examples.stem: The child _____ playing in the yard is my son.
examples.why_en: playing is an adjective (no be before it). The sentence already has subject child and verb is. Do not add is/was/he. now fits as an adverb.
examples.why_id: playing = adjective (tidak ada be di depannya). Subject child dan verb is sudah lengkap. Jangan tambah is/was/he. now cocok sebagai adverb.

examples.stem: The technician _____ the calibration logs noticed a recurring error.
examples.why_en: reviewing = present participle adjective (who was reviewing). Main verb = noticed.
examples.why_id: reviewing = present participle sebagai adjective (who was reviewing). Verb utama = noticed.

examples.stem: _____ the safety checklist, the pilot requested clearance for departure.
examples.why_en: Completing… = reduced adverbial (While/After completing…). Present participle opens the clause.
examples.why_id: Completing… = reduced adverbial (While/After completing…). Present participle membuka klausa.

checklist_id: Temukan semua kata -ing.
Cek: apakah ada be (is/are/was/were) tepat sebelumnya?
Jika ya → bagian verb. Jika tidak → kemungkinan adjective.
Cari finite verb lain (is, has, was, noticed…).
Jangan menambah subject/verb ekstra jika S + V sudah lengkap.
checklist_en: Find every -ing word.
Check: is there be (is/are/was/were) right before it?
If yes → part of the verb. If no → likely an adjective.
Find another finite verb (is, has, was, noticed…).
Do not add an extra subject/verb if S + V is already complete.
remember_id: **be + V-ing** = verb. **V-ing tanpa be** = sering adjective. Pastikan kalimat punya finite verb yang sesungguhnya.
remember_en: **be + V-ing** = verb. **V-ing without be** = often an adjective. Make sure the sentence has a real finite verb.

summary_id: Past participle (sering -ed, atau irregular) bisa bagian verb (dengan have/be) atau adjective (tanpa have/be). Jangan dikira verb utama jika hanya modifier.
summary_en: A past participle (often -ed, or irregular) can be part of the verb (with have/be) or an adjective (without have/be). Do not treat it as the main verb when it is only a modifier.

formula.label: Sebagai bagian VERB
formula.en:
have/has/had + V3
be (is/are/was…) + V3
The family has purchased a television.
The poem was written by Paul.
formula.id:
have/has/had + V3
be (is/are/was…) + V3
The family has purchased a television.
The poem was written by Paul.

formula.label: Sebagai ADJECTIVE
formula.en:
Noun + V3 …  (no have/be before it)
The television purchased yesterday was expensive.
→ purchased = adjective; main verb = was
formula.id:
Noun + V3 …  (tanpa have/be di depannya)
The television purchased yesterday was expensive.
→ purchased = adjective; verb utama = was

formula.label: Tiga peran bentuk -ed
formula.en:
1) Simple past: She painted this picture.
2) Past participle (verb): She has painted…
3) Adjective: The picture painted by Karen is…
formula.id:
1) Simple past: She painted this picture.
2) Past participle (verb): She has painted…
3) Adjective: The picture painted by Karen is…

rules.body_id: Bentuk verb yang muncul bersama have atau be. Sering berakhir -ed, tapi banyak yang irregular (written, bought, found…).
rules.body_en: The verb form that appears with have or be. It often ends in -ed, but many are irregular (written, bought, found…).

rules.title_en: 2. With have/be = part of the verb
rules.body_id: has purchased, was written → past participle melengkapi verb phrase. Jangan bingung dengan adjective.
rules.body_en: has purchased, was written → the past participle completes the verb phrase. Do not confuse it with an adjective use.

rules.body_id: Jika tidak ada have/be tepat sebelumnya, dan ada finite verb lain di kalimat, V3 biasanya reduced relative (adjective).
rules.body_en: If there is no have/be right before it, and another finite verb exists in the sentence, V3 is usually a reduced relative (adjective).

rules.title_id: 4. Jangan menambah helping verb yang tidak perlu
rules.title_en: 4. Do not add an unnecessary helping verb
rules.body_id: Jika mailed/written/purchased hanya adjective, opsi have/were sering salah. Cari verb utama yang sudah ada (will arrive, was, appeared…).
rules.body_en: If mailed/written/purchased is only an adjective, options like have/were are often wrong. Find the main verb already in the sentence (will arrive, was, appeared…).

examples.stem: The packages _____ mailed at the post office will arrive Monday.
examples.why_en: mailed is a participial adjective (no have/be before it). Main verb = will arrive. just fits as an adverb. have/were wrongly treat mailed as needing a helper; them is an extra object.
examples.why_id: mailed = adjective (tidak ada have/be di depan). Verb utama = will arrive. just cocok sebagai adverb. have/were salah menganggap mailed butuh helper; them = object ekstra.

examples.stem: The report _____ on the director's desk summarizes last quarter's findings.
examples.why_en: placed = past participle adjective (which was placed). Main verb = summarizes.
examples.why_id: placed = past participle adjective (which was placed). Verb utama = summarizes.

examples.stem: _____ by successive budget cuts, the program suspended field operations.
examples.why_en: Weakened by… = reduced passive (Because it was weakened…). Past participle opens the clause.
examples.why_id: Weakened by… = reduced passive (Because it was weakened…). Past participle membuka klausa.

checklist_id: Temukan bentuk V3 / -ed / irregular participle.
Cek: ada have atau be tepat sebelumnya?
Jika ya → bagian verb. Jika tidak → kemungkinan adjective.
Cari finite verb lain di kalimat (will arrive, was, appeared…).
Jangan menambah have/were/them jika S + V sudah lengkap.
checklist_en: Find every V3 / -ed / irregular participle.
Check: is there have or be right before it?
If yes → part of the verb. If no → likely an adjective.
Find another finite verb (will arrive, was, appeared…).
Do not add have/were/them if S + V is already complete.
remember_id: **have/be + V3** = verb. **V3 tanpa have/be** = sering adjective. Pastikan ada finite verb yang sesungguhnya.
remember_en: **have/be + V3** = verb. **V3 without have/be** = often an adjective. Make sure there is a real finite verb.

summary_id: Dua independent clause harus dihubungkan dengan benar. Coordinate connectors: and, but, or, so, yet (biasanya dengan koma).
summary_en: Two independent clauses must be joined correctly. Coordinate connectors: and, but, or, so, yet (usually with a comma).

formula.label: Pola dasar
formula.en:
S V ,  coordinate connector  S V
She laughed, but she wanted to cry.
formula.id:
S V ,  coordinate connector  S V
She laughed, but she wanted to cry.

formula.label: Daftar connector
formula.en:
and  (addition)
but / yet  (contrast)
or  (choice)
so  (result)
formula.id:
and  (tambahan)
but / yet  (kontras)
or  (pilihan)
so  (hasil/akibat)

formula.label: Bukan connector
formula.en:
then, later, next, after that → NOT coordinate connectors alone
They cannot join two full clauses by themselves on TOEFL Structure.
formula.id:
then, later, next, after that → BUKAN coordinate connector
Tidak bisa sendiri menghubungkan dua clause penuh di Structure TOEFL.

rules.body_id: Jika ada lebih dari satu clause, pastikan tiap clause punya subject dan verb, lalu dihubungkan dengan connector yang tepat.
rules.body_en: If there is more than one clause, each clause needs a subject and a verb, then a correct connector between them.

rules.body_id: and, but, or, so, yet. Contoh: Tom is singing, and Paul is dancing. Tom is tired, yet he is not going to sleep.
rules.body_en: and, but, or, so, yet. Example: Tom is singing, and Paul is dancing. Tom is tired, yet he is not going to sleep.

rules.body_id: and = tambah; but/yet = kontras; or = pilihan; so = akibat. Pilih sesuai hubungan logika dua clause.
rules.body_en: and = addition; but/yet = contrast; or = choice; so = result. Match the logic between the two clauses.

rules.title_en: 4. then / later / next are not enough
rules.body_id: Kata urutan waktu saja tidak menghubungkan dua independent clause di pola coordinate. Butuh and/but/or/so/yet (atau struktur lain di skill berikutnya).
rules.body_en: Time-sequence words alone do not join two independent clauses in this coordinate pattern. You need and/but/or/so/yet (or another structure in later skills).

examples.stem: A power failure occurred, _____ the lamps went out.
examples.why_en: Two clauses need a real coordinate connector. so joins them with a result meaning. then/later/next are not coordinate connectors here.
examples.why_id: Dua clause butuh coordinate connector sejati. so menghubungkan dengan makna akibat. then/later/next bukan coordinate connector di pola ini.

examples.stem: The pilot succeeded on several metrics, _____ national scale-up remains premature without longer follow-up.
examples.why_en: Contrast between success and remaining limits → but.
examples.why_id: Kontras antara keberhasilan dan batasan yang tersisa → but.

examples.stem: The sampling frame must be complete, _____ population totals will be biased.
examples.why_en: Result relationship → so (if incomplete… totals will be biased / completeness required so that totals are not biased — here so marks the result clause).
examples.why_id: Hubungan akibat → so.

checklist_id: Hitung berapa clause (berapa pasangan subject + verb).
Cek apakah clause sudah dihubungkan.
Pakai and / but / or / so / yet sesuai makna.
Jangan andalkan then / later / next sebagai satu-satunya penghubung.
Pastikan koma + connector di antara dua independent clause.
checklist_en: Count the clauses (subject + verb pairs).
Check whether the clauses are joined.
Use and / but / or / so / yet for the right meaning.
Do not rely on then / later / next as the only link.
Use comma + connector between two independent clauses.
remember_id: Dua clause: **S V , + and/but/or/so/yet + S V**. then/later/next bukan coordinate connector.
remember_en: Two clauses: **S V , + and/but/or/so/yet + S V**. then/later/next are not coordinate connectors.

title_en: Use adverb time and cause connectors correctly
title_id: Gunakan connector waktu & sebab dengan benar
summary_id: Adverb clause waktu/sebab punya subject + verb dan connector (when, because, since…). Dua pola: connector di tengah (tanpa koma) atau di awal (pakai koma).
summary_en: Time/cause adverb clauses need subject + verb and a connector (when, because, since…). Two patterns: connector in the middle (no comma) or at the beginning (comma required).

formula.label: Pola 1 — connector di tengah
formula.en:
S V   + adverb connector +   S V
Teresa went inside because it was raining.
(no comma)
formula.id:
S V   + adverb connector +   S V
Teresa went inside because it was raining.
(tanpa koma)

formula.label: Pola 2 — connector di awal
formula.en:
Adverb connector + S V ,  S V
Because it was raining, Teresa went inside.
(comma after the adverb clause)
formula.id:
Adverb connector + S V ,  S V
Because it was raining, Teresa went inside.
(koma setelah adverb clause)

formula.label: TIME vs CAUSE
formula.en:
TIME: after, before, when, while, until, as soon as, once, by the time, as long as, whenever, since (time)

rules.title_id: 2. Setelah connector harus ada subject + verb

title_id: Gunakan noun clause connector dengan benar
summary_id: Noun clause = clause yang berfungsi sebagai noun (object verb, object preposition, atau subject). Connector: that, what, when, whether, if, how…
summary_en: A noun clause functions as a noun (object of a verb, object of a preposition, or subject). Connectors: that, what, when, whether, if, how…

formula.label: Sebagai OBJECT of verb
formula.en:
S V + noun connector + S V
I know what you did.
I know when he will arrive.
formula.id:

I know when he will arrive.

… preposition + noun connector + S V

formula.id:
… preposition + noun connector + S V

Noun connector + S V  +  V …

That he was late caused many problems.
formula.id:
Noun connector + S V  +  V …

rules.title_en: 1. A noun clause acts as a noun
rules.body_id: Bisa jadi object of verb, object of preposition, atau subject kalimat. Tetap punya subject + verb di dalamnya.
rules.body_en: It can be object of a verb, object of a preposition, or subject of the sentence. It still has its own subject + verb inside.

rules.body_id: what, when, where, why, how · whatever, whenever · whether, if · that
rules.body_en: what, when, where, why, how · whatever, whenever · whether, if · that

rules.body_id: That he was late caused many problems. → that he was late = subject dari caused. Opsi The driver hanya satu subject — tidak cukup jika butuh subject untuk was dan untuk caused.
rules.body_en: That he was late caused many problems. → that he was late = subject of caused. The driver is only one subject — not enough when both was and caused need subjects.

rules.body_id: Di noun clause, pakai urutan statement: when he will arrive (bukan when will he arrive).
rules.body_en: Inside a noun clause, use statement order: when he will arrive (not when will he arrive).

examples.stem: _____ was late caused many problems.
examples.why_en: was and caused each need a subject. That he → he is subject of was; That he was late is the subject of caused. The driver is only one subject. There / Because are not subjects for this pattern.
examples.why_id: was dan caused masing-masing butuh subject. That he → he subject of was; That he was late subject of caused. The driver hanya satu subject. There / Because tidak cocok.

examples.stem: Scientists are now beginning to conduct experiments on _____ trigger different sorts of health risks.
examples.why_en: Noun clause object of on: how noise pollution can trigger… needs connector + subject + verb.
examples.why_id: Noun clause object of on: how noise pollution can trigger… butuh connector + subject + verb.

examples.stem: It remains unclear _____ the instrument satisfies the exclusion restriction.
examples.why_en: whether = yes/no uncertainty as noun clause connector.
examples.why_id: whether = ketidakpastian ya/tidak sebagai noun clause connector.

checklist_id: Identifikasi fungsi: object verb / object preposition / subject.
Setelah connector noun clause → subject + verb (kecuali connector/subject di S10).
that / whether / what / how… sesuai makna.
Subject noun clause → verb utama di luar clause tetap ada.
Tidak invert di embedded clause.
checklist_en: Identify role: object of verb / object of preposition / subject.
After the noun-clause connector → subject + verb (unless connector/subject in S10).
that / whether / what / how… for the right meaning.
If the noun clause is subject, the main verb still follows.
No inversion in the embedded clause.
remember_id: Noun clause = **connector + S + V**, berfungsi seperti noun (object atau subject).
remember_en: A noun clause = **connector + S + V**, used like a noun (object or subject).

title_id: Gunakan noun clause connector/subject dengan benar
summary_id: Kadang connector noun clause juga menjadi subject clause itu sendiri: what, who, which, whatever, whoever, whichever.
summary_en: Sometimes the noun-clause connector is also the subject of that clause: what, who, which, whatever, whoever, whichever.

formula.label: Sebagai OBJECT
formula.en:
S V + connector/subject + V
I know what happened.
(what = subject of happened + connector)
formula.id:
S V + connector/subject + V
I know what happened.
(what = subject of happened + connector)

formula.label: Sebagai SUBJECT kalimat
formula.en:
Connector/subject + V  +  V …
What happened was great.
Whoever is coming to the party must bring a gift.
formula.id:
Connector/subject + V  +  V …
What happened was great.
Whoever is coming to the party must bring a gift.

formula.en:
who, what, which
whoever, whatever, whichever

rules.body_id: what / who / whoever = connector sekaligus subject di clause dalamnya. Tidak perlu subject ekstra setelahnya.
rules.body_en: what / who / whoever = connector and subject inside the clause. Do not add another subject after it.

rules.body_id: S9: I know what you did → what + subject you + verb did. S10: I know what happened → what langsung + verb (what = subject).
rules.body_en: S9: I know what you did → what + subject you + verb did. S10: I know what happened → what + verb (what is the subject).

rules.title_id: 3. Dua verb = dua subject (bisa dari noun clause)
rules.body_id: was on television made me angry → butuh subject untuk was dan untuk made. What mengisi keduanya: what was… = subject of made; what = subject of was.
rules.body_en: was on television made me angry → need a subject for was and for made. What covers both: what was… = subject of made; what = subject of was.

rules.title_en: 4. when / it are not this pattern
rules.body_id: when bukan subject. it / the story tidak bisa jadi subject untuk dua verb sekaligus dalam pola ini.
rules.body_en: when is not a subject. it / the story cannot be the subject of both verbs in this pattern.

examples.stem: _____ was on television made me angry.
examples.why_en: was and made each need a subject. What is subject of was and joins the clauses; what was on television is subject of made. It / The story cannot serve both verbs. When is not a subject.
examples.why_id: was dan made masing-masing butuh subject. What = subject of was + connector; what was on television = subject of made. It / The story tidak cukup untuk keduanya. When bukan subject.

examples.stem: _____ remains most contested is whether the estimate travels beyond the sample.

examples.why_id: What remains contested = noun clause subject of is.

examples.stem: _____ decides the primary endpoint should do so before outcomes are seen.

examples.why_id: Whoever decides… = connector/subject of decides dan subject of should do.

checklist_id: Cek apakah connector juga subject (what/who/whoever + V langsung).
Hitung verb: tiap verb butuh subject.
Jangan dobel subject (what it was…).
when/it biasanya salah di pola connector/subject.
Bedakan S9 (connector + S + V) vs S10 (connector/subject + V).
checklist_en: Check whether the connector is also the subject (what/who/whoever + V).

when/it are usually wrong in this connector/subject pattern.

remember_id: **what/who/whoever + V** — connector sekaligus subject. Satu kata menghubungkan clause dan mengisi subject.

title_id: Gunakan adjective clause connector dengan benar
summary_id: Adjective clause menjelaskan noun dan langsung mengikuti noun itu. Connector: who/whom (orang), which (benda), that (orang/benda). Di dalam clause tetap ada subject + verb.
summary_en: An adjective clause describes a noun and sits right after it. Connectors: who/whom (people), which (things), that (people or things). Inside the clause there is still subject + verb.

formula.label: Pola dasar
formula.en:
Noun + adjective connector + S V …
I liked the book which you recommended.
The book which you recommended was interesting.
formula.id:
Noun + adjective connector + S V …
I liked the book which you recommended.
The book which you recommended was interesting.

formula.label: Connector
formula.en:
whom  → people (object)
which → things
that  → people or things
formula.id:
whom  → orang (object)
which → benda
that  → orang atau benda

formula.en:
Two clauses → need connector + subject for the second clause.
which we selected  ✓
because / since without subject  ✗

Dua clause → butuh connector + subject di clause kedua.
which we selected  ✓

rules.body_id: The glass that she put on the table contains milk. Clause that she put on the table menjelaskan glass.

rules.body_id: Salah: The movie which we watched it was frightening. Benar: The movie which we watched was frightening.
rules.body_en: Wrong: The movie which we watched it was frightening. Right: The movie which we watched was frightening.

examples.stem: The gift _____ selected for the bride was rather expensive.

examples.why_id: gift subject of was; selected butuh subject → which we selected. because/since tanpa subject; was menambah verb tanpa memperbaiki clause kedua.

whom = orang object; which = benda; that = keduanya.

summary_id: Adjective clause bisa diringkas: hilangkan connector/subject + be, atau ubah verb jadi -ing. Hanya jika connector langsung diikuti verb (connector = subject).
summary_en: Adjective clauses can reduce: drop connector/subject + be, or change the verb to -ing. Only when the connector is directly followed by a verb (connector = subject).

that is on the table → on the table

which was written → written
that is on the table → on the table

checklist_id: Connector langsung diikuti verb? Jika tidak → jangan reduce.
Ada be? → hilangkan connector + be.
Tidak ada be? → hilangkan connector, ubah verb ke -ing.
Dengan koma? → reduced bisa dipindah ke depan.
Jangan pakai who appeared… (lengkap) di awal kalimat.
checklist_en: Is the connector directly followed by a verb? If not → do not reduce.
Is there be? → drop connector + be.
No be? → drop connector, change verb to -ing.
Set off with commas? → reduced form can move to the front.
Do not put full who appeared… at the start of the sentence.

summary_en: Adverb clauses can reduce: keep the connector, drop subject (+ be); or drop subject and change the verb to -ing. Not every connector reduces in both active and passive.

Although he feels sick → Although feeling sick
When you give your speech → When giving your speech

formula.label: Aktif vs pasif
formula.en:
after/before/while… → often reduce in ACTIVE
once/until/when… → may reduce mainly in PASSIVE
Once submitted, your thesis will be reviewed. ✓
Once you submit… (active) often does not reduce the same way.
formula.id:
after/before/while… → sering reduce di AKTIF
once/until/when… → sering reduce di PASIF
Once submitted, your thesis will be reviewed. ✓

rules.body_id: Berbeda dengan reduced adjective clause, di reduced adverb clause connector (when, although, if…) tetap ditulis.
rules.body_en: Unlike reduced adjective clauses, in reduced adverb clauses the connector (when, although, if…) remains.

rules.body_id: When finished with the report, you are free to leave. = When you are finished…
rules.body_en: When finished with the report, you are free to leave. = When you are finished…

rules.body_id: Beberapa connector hanya reduce jika verb pasif (once submitted). Bentuk aktif once you submit sering tidak di-reduce.
rules.body_en: Some connectors reduce mainly with passive verbs (once submitted). Active once you submit often does not reduce.

rules.title_id: 4. Setelah connector jangan hanya noun tanpa struktur reduced
rules.title_en: 4. Do not leave a bare noun after the connector
rules.body_id: When the finished report ✗ · When finished with the report ✓ · When is the report finished ✗ (bukan pertanyaan di sini).
rules.body_en: When the finished report ✗ · When finished with the report ✓ · When is the report finished ✗ (not a question here).

examples.stem: When _____, you are free to leave.
examples.why_en: finished with the report is the reduced form of when you are finished with the report. Bare nouns lack the reduced structure; inversion is wrong here.
examples.why_id: finished with the report = reduced dari when you are finished with the report. Noun saja kurang; inversion salah di sini.

examples.stem: Kokanee salmon begin to die soon _____ at about four years of age.
examples.why_en: after spawning = reduced time clause (after they spawn).
examples.why_id: after spawning = reduced time clause (after they spawn).

examples.stem: _____ only a light sweater, she stepped out into the rain.
examples.why_en: Wearing… = reduced (While she was wearing…). Present participle reduction.
examples.why_id: Wearing… = reduced (While she was wearing…).

checklist_id: Connector adverb tetap ada (when/although/if…).
Subject (+ be) dihilangkan, atau verb diubah ke -ing.
Cek apakah connector ini boleh reduce aktif/pasif.
Jangan sisakan noun saja setelah connector.
Beda dari S13: di S14 connector tidak dihapus.
checklist_en: The adverb connector stays (when/although/if…).
Drop subject (+ be), or change the verb to -ing.
Check whether this connector reduces in active/passive.
Do not leave a bare noun after the connector.
Unlike S13: in S14 the connector is not deleted.
remember_id: Reduced adverb: **connector tetap** + (tanpa subject/be) atau **-ing**. When finished… ✓ · When the report… ✗
remember_en: Reduced adverb: **connector stays** + (no subject/be) or **-ing**. When finished… ✓ · When the report… ✗

title_en: Invert the subject and verb with question words
group_en: Sentences with Inverted Subjects and Verbs
summary_id: what/when/where/why/how: jika pertanyaan → invert. Jika menghubungkan dua clause (embedded) → JANGAN invert (subject lalu verb).
summary_en: what/when/where/why/how: in a real question → invert. When joining two clauses (embedded) → do NOT invert (subject then verb).

formula.label: Pertanyaan → INVERT
formula.en:
question word + V + S ?
What are they?
Where are you going?
formula.id:
question word + V + S ?
What are they?
Where are you going?

formula.label: Embedded (bukan pertanyaan) → TIDAK invert
formula.en:
S V + question word + S V
I know what they are.
The lawyer asked why he did it.
formula.id:
S V + question word + S V
I know what they are.
The lawyer asked why he did it.

formula.label: Cek cepat
formula.en:
Is it a real question ending with ?
YES → invert
NO (I know / asked / explain why…) → subject + verb order
formula.id:
Apakah pertanyaan sungguhan (ada ?)?
YA → invert
TIDAK (I know / asked / explain why…) → subject + verb

rules.body_id: Bisa membuka pertanyaan (invert) atau menghubungkan dua clause (tidak invert).
rules.body_en: They can open a question (invert) or join two clauses (no invert).

rules.body_id: why he did it ✓ · why did he do it ✗ (bukan pertanyaan). when the vault will be opened ✓ · when will the vault… ✗ di noun clause.
rules.body_en: why he did it ✓ · why did he do it ✗ (not a question). when the vault will be opened ✓ · when will the vault… ✗ in a noun clause.

rules.body_id: Clause setelahnya hampir selalu embedded → tidak invert.
rules.body_en: The clause after these verbs is almost always embedded → no inversion.

rules.body_id: Where is it cheapest…? How long has it been…? → invert karena pertanyaan sungguhan.
rules.body_en: Where is it cheapest…? How long has it been…? → invert because these are real questions.

examples.stem: The lawyer asked the client why _____ it.
examples.why_en: why joins two clauses (not a question) → he did (subject + verb). did he do is inverted and wrong here.
examples.why_id: why menghubungkan dua clause (bukan pertanyaan) → he did. did he do = invert, salah di sini.

examples.stem: There are several reasons why _____ across cultures.
examples.why_en: Embedded why-clause: why + subject + verb → eating habits differ.
examples.why_id: Embedded why-clause: why + subject + verb → eating habits differ.

examples.stem: Only the pilot can tell you how far _____ on one tank of fuel.
examples.why_en: After tell you how far… this is embedded → the plane can go (no inversion).
examples.why_id: Setelah tell you how far… ini embedded → the plane can go (tidak invert).

checklist_id: Question word di pertanyaan sungguhan? → invert.
Question word menghubungkan clause (know/ask/why…)? → jangan invert.
Urutan embedded: question word + subject + verb.
Hindari did he / can the plane di noun clause.
Cek tanda tanya di akhir kalimat.
checklist_en: Question word in a real question? → invert.
Question word joining clauses (know/ask/why…)? → do not invert.
Embedded order: question word + subject + verb.
Avoid did he / can the plane inside a noun clause.
Check whether the sentence ends with a question mark.
remember_id: **Pertanyaan → invert.** **Embedded (I know why…) → subject + verb.** why **he did** it ✓
remember_en: **Question → invert.** **Embedded (I know why…) → subject + verb.** why **he did** it ✓

title_en: Invert the subject and verb with place expressions
group_en: Sentences with Inverted Subjects and Verbs
summary_id: Place di depan (here, there, in the closet, beyond the mountains…) → invert **hanya jika** place expression diperlukan untuk melengkapi makna kalimat.
summary_en: Place first (here, there, in the closet, beyond the mountains…) → invert **only if** the place expression is needed to complete the sentence meaning.

formula.label: Place perlu → INVERT
formula.en:
PLACE + V + S
In the classroom were some old desks.
Here is the book that you lent me.
formula.id:
PLACE + V + S
In the classroom were some old desks.
Here is the book that you lent me.

formula.label: Place hanya info ekstra → TIDAK invert
formula.en:
PLACE , S V
In the classroom, I studied very hard.
(I studied is complete without the place phrase)
formula.id:
PLACE , S V
In the classroom, I studied very hard.
(I studied sudah lengkap tanpa place phrase)

formula.label: Contoh kata/frase
formula.en:
here, there, nowhere
in the closet, around the corner, beyond the mountains, on the second level…
formula.id:
here, there, nowhere
in the closet, around the corner, beyond the mountains, on the second level…

rules.body_id: Here is the book… · There are the keys… · In the closet are the clothes… · Beyond the mountains lies the town…
rules.body_en: Here is the book… · There are the keys… · In the closet are the clothes… · Beyond the mountains lies the town…

rules.body_id: In the forest are many exotic birds. (birds are… butuh place). In the forest I walked for many hours. (I walked sudah lengkap → tidak invert).
rules.body_en: In the forest are many exotic birds. (birds are… needs place). In the forest I walked for many hours. (I walked is complete → no invert).

rules.body_id: are some empty stalls ✓ · some empty stalls are ✗ setelah place expression yang necessary.
rules.body_en: are some empty stalls ✓ · some empty stalls are ✗ after a necessary place expression.

rules.body_id: Across the valley lie several settlements (plural). On the wall hangs a map (singular).
rules.body_en: Across the valley lie several settlements (plural). On the wall hangs a map (singular).

examples.stem: On the second level of the parking lot _____.
examples.why_en: Place expression is necessary to complete the idea. Need inverted V + S → are some empty stalls.
examples.why_id: Place expression diperlukan untuk melengkapi ide. Butuh invert V + S → are some empty stalls.

examples.stem: Located behind the two lacrimal glands _____.
examples.why_en: Fronted place/participle structure → invert: is each eyelid.
examples.why_id: Place/participle di depan → invert: is each eyelid.

examples.stem: Across the plain _____ a few isolated farmhouses.
examples.why_en: Place fronted; subject farmhouses is plural → stand.
examples.why_id: Place di depan; subject farmhouses plural → stand.

checklist_id: Ada place expression di depan kalimat?
Apakah place itu necessary untuk melengkapi S+V?
Jika ya → verb + subject (invert).
Jika tidak (hanya ekstra) → subject + verb biasa.
Cocokkan singular/plural subject dengan verb.
checklist_en: Is there a place expression at the front?
Is that place necessary to complete S+V?
If yes → verb + subject (invert).
If not (only extra) → normal subject + verb.
Match singular/plural subject with the verb.
remember_id: Place di depan + **perlu** → **V + S**. Place hanya ekstra → **S + V**. are some empty stalls ✓
remember_en: Place first + **necessary** → **V + S**. Place only extra → **S + V**. are some empty stalls ✓

title_en: Invert the subject and verb with negatives
group_en: Sentences with Inverted Subjects and Verbs
summary_id: Negatif / almost-negative di depan (never, not only, rarely, only once, neither, nor…) → subject dan verb di-invert (auxiliary + subject + main verb).
summary_en: A negative / almost-negative at the front (never, not only, rarely, only once, neither, nor…) → invert subject and verb (auxiliary + subject + main verb).

formula.label: Pola invert
formula.en:
Negative expression + auxiliary + S + (main verb)
Never has Mr. Jones taken a vacation.
Only once did the manager issue overtime paychecks.
formula.id:
Negative expression + auxiliary + S + (main verb)
Never has Mr. Jones taken a vacation.
Only once did the manager issue overtime paychecks.

formula.label: Negatif & almost-negative
formula.en:
no, not, never, neither, nor
barely, hardly, only, rarely, scarcely, seldom
formula.id:
no, not, never, neither, nor
barely, hardly, only, rarely, scarcely, seldom

formula.label: Di tengah kalimat juga
formula.en:
…, and neither does Tom.
…, nor is her boss.
formula.id:
…, and neither does Tom.
…, nor is her boss.

rules.body_id: Not once did I miss a question. Never has Mr. Jones taken a vacation. At no time can the woman talk on the phone.
rules.body_en: Not once did I miss a question. Never has Mr. Jones taken a vacation. At no time can the woman talk on the phone.

rules.body_id: hardly ever, barely, scarcely, only once, rarely, seldom di depan → invert juga.
rules.body_en: hardly ever, barely, scarcely, only once, rarely, seldom at the front → also invert.

rules.body_id: I do not want to go, and neither does Tom. … nor did he expect to. Setelah neither/nor → invert.
rules.body_en: I do not want to go, and neither does Tom. … nor did he expect to. After neither/nor → invert.

rules.body_id: will the printing presses be stopped ✓ · the printing presses will be ✗ · will be the printing presses ✗ (urutan aux-subject-verb).
rules.body_en: will the printing presses be stopped ✓ · the printing presses will be ✗ · will be the printing presses ✗ (order: aux-subject-verb).

examples.stem: Only in extremely dangerous situations _____ stopped.
options: that the printing presses will be
examples.why_en: Only… at the front requires inversion: will the printing presses be stopped.
examples.why_id: Only… di depan wajib invert: will the printing presses be stopped.

examples.stem: Rarely _____ located near city lights or at lower elevations.
examples.why_en: Rarely + inversion: are observatories located…
examples.why_id: Rarely + inversion: are observatories located…

examples.stem: Never in the world _____ that this would happen.
examples.why_en: Never… → did I believe (aux + subject + verb).
examples.why_id: Never… → did I believe (aux + subject + verb).

checklist_id: Ada never/not/only/rarely/neither/nor di depan clause?
Jika ya → auxiliary + subject + main verb.
Jangan biarkan subject di depan setelah negatif (Never the boy wrote…).
neither/nor di tengah juga invert.
Urutan: will the presses be… bukan will be the presses…
checklist_en: Is there never/not/only/rarely/neither/nor before the clause?
If yes → auxiliary + subject + main verb.
Do not leave subject first after a negative (Never the boy wrote…).
neither/nor mid-sentence also invert.
Order: will the presses be… not will be the presses…
remember_id: Negatif di depan → **aux + S + V**. Only… **will the printing presses be** stopped ✓
remember_en: Negative first → **aux + S + V**. Only… **will the printing presses be** stopped ✓

title_en: Invert the subject and verb with conditionals
group_en: Sentences with Inverted Subjects and Verbs
summary_id: Conditional dengan had / should / were: bisa pakai if (urutan normal) atau hilangkan if lalu invert (Had he taken… / Were I… / Should you arrive…).
summary_en: Conditionals with had / should / were: keep if (normal order) or omit if and invert (Had he taken… / Were I… / Should you arrive…).

formula.label: Dengan if (tidak invert)
formula.en:
if + S + had/should/were …
If he had taken more time, the results would have been better.
formula.id:
if + S + had/should/were …
If he had taken more time, the results would have been better.

formula.label: Tanpa if (invert)
formula.en:
Had / Should / Were + S …
Had he taken more time, the results would have been better.
Were I in a position to help, I would help you.
Should you arrive before 6:00, just give me a call.
formula.id:
Had / Should / Were + S …
Had he taken more time…
Were I in a position to help…
Should you arrive before 6:00…

formula.label: Verb yang boleh invert
formula.en:
had · should · were
(not every conditional inverts — mainly these three)
formula.id:
had · should · were
(bukan semua conditional — terutama ketiga ini)

rules.title_en: 1. Two ways to write the conditional
rules.body_id: If he had taken more time… = Had he taken more time… Makna sama; yang kedua tanpa if + invert.
rules.body_en: If he had taken more time… = Had he taken more time… Same meaning; the second omits if and inverts.

rules.body_id: Pola invert conditional klasik memakai helping verb had, should, atau were di depan subject.
rules.body_en: Classic inverted conditionals put helping verb had, should, or were before the subject.

rules.body_id: had more care been taken ✓ · more care had been taken (tanpa if) kurang tepat di pola invert · if more care (tanpa verb) ✗ · had taken more care (subject hilang/tergeser) ✗
rules.body_en: had more care been taken ✓ · more care had been taken (no if) is not the inverted pattern · if more care (no verb) ✗ · had taken more care (subject misplaced) ✗

rules.body_id: Invert hanya di conditional clause. the results would have been better tetap S + V.
rules.body_en: Invert only in the conditional clause. the results would have been better stays S + V.

examples.stem: The report would have been accepted _____ in checking its accuracy.
examples.why_en: Omit if and invert: had more care been taken. (A) has if + no verb. (B) has no if and no inversion. (C) misplaces the subject.
examples.why_id: Hilangkan if lalu invert: had more care been taken. (A) if tanpa verb. (B) tanpa if dan tanpa invert. (C) subject salah posisi.

examples.stem: _____ milk test positive on arrival, the whole tanker load must be discarded.
examples.why_en: Should milk test positive… = inverted conditional (If milk should test / If milk tests…).
examples.why_id: Should milk test positive… = inverted conditional.

examples.stem: _____ the authors known about the error before submission, the tables would have changed.
examples.why_en: Had the authors known… = If the authors had known…
examples.why_id: Had the authors known… = If the authors had known…

checklist_id: Conditional dengan had/should/were?
Ada if? → urutan normal S + V.
Tanpa if? → Had/Should/Were + subject + …
Subject jangan hilang atau tertukar (had more care been taken).
Invert hanya di if-clause, bukan di main clause.
checklist_en: Conditional with had/should/were?
Is if present? → normal S + V order.
No if? → Had/Should/Were + subject + …
Do not drop or misplace the subject (had more care been taken).
Invert only in the if-clause, not the main clause.
remember_id: **Had / Should / Were + S …** = if-clause tanpa if. **Had more care been taken** ✓
remember_en: **Had / Should / Were + S …** = if-clause without if. **Had more care been taken** ✓

title_en: Invert the subject and verb with comparisons
group_en: Sentences with Inverted Subjects and Verbs
summary_id: Setelah comparison (more…than, as…as), subject–verb boleh di-invert (opsional, formal). than does John / than were they — keduanya bisa benar.
summary_en: After a comparison (more…than, as…as), subject–verb inversion is optional and formal. than does John / than were they — both can be correct.

formula.label: Tiga bentuk yang benar
formula.en:
…more hours than John.
…more hours than John does.
…more hours than does John.  ← inverted (formal)
formula.id:
…more hours than John.
…more hours than John does.
…more hours than does John.  ← inverted (formal)

formula.label: Pola invert
formula.en:
S V comparison + V + S
We were more prepared than were the other performers.
formula.id:
S V comparison + V + S
We were more prepared than were the other performers.

formula.label: Pola normal (juga benar)
formula.en:
S V comparison + S + V
We were more prepared than the other performers were.
formula.id:
S V comparison + S + V
We were more prepared than the other performers were.

rules.body_id: Berbeda dengan never/only (wajib invert), setelah than/as invert bersifat formal dan pilihan.
rules.body_en: Unlike never/only (required inversion), after than/as inversion is formal and optional.

rules.body_id: the results of the current experiment vs the results of any previous tests. Setelah than butuh verb yang cocok (were), bukan them.
rules.body_en: the results of the current experiment vs the results of any previous tests. After than you need a fitting verb (were), not them.

rules.body_id: than were the results of any previous tests — verb dulu agar subject panjang tidak terasa berat di tengah.
rules.body_en: than were the results of any previous tests — verb first so a long subject is easier to process.

rules.title_id: 4. Jangan object pronoun sebagai pengganti clause
rules.title_en: 4. Do not use a bare object pronoun for the clause
rules.body_id: more consistent than them ✗ jika yang dibandingkan adalah full subject + verb idea. than they were / than were they ✓
rules.body_en: more consistent than them ✗ when you need a full subject + verb idea. than they were / than were they ✓

examples.stem: The results of the current experiment appear to be more consistent than _____ the results of any previous tests.
examples.why_en: The blank is followed by the subject the results of any previous tests, so you need a verb before it: were (inverted). them is not a verb. they were / were they would require the pronoun they, but the full noun phrase is already written after the blank.
examples.why_id: Setelah blank sudah ada subject the results of any previous tests, jadi butuh verb di depan: were (invert). them bukan verb. they were / were they memakai they, padahal noun phrase lengkap sudah tertulis setelah blank.

examples.stem: New York City's Central Park is nearly twice as large _____ second-smallest country, Monaco.
examples.why_en: as is the second-smallest country — comparative with optional inversion-like parallel structure.
examples.why_id: as is the second-smallest country — struktur parallel comparison.

examples.stem: The revised model fits the validation sample far better than _____ the original linear specification.
examples.why_en: than does + subject (inverted) is the formal pattern; (C) non-inverted is also grammatical, but (B) matches the inverted comparison skill focus.
examples.why_id: than does + subject (inverted) = pola formal skill ini.

checklist_id: Ada comparison (more/than, as…as)?
Invert opsional: than does John / than John does sama-sama bisa.
Subject yang dibandingkan harus sejajar.
Hindari them jika butuh subject + verb.
Pola invert: than + aux/verb + subject.
checklist_en: Is there a comparison (more/than, as…as)?
Inversion optional: than does John / than John does both work.
Compared subjects should be parallel.
Avoid them when you need subject + verb.
Inverted pattern: than + aux/verb + subject.
remember_id: Comparison: invert **opsional & formal**. **than were the other performers** / **than does John** ✓
remember_en: Comparison: inversion is **optional & formal**. **than were the other performers** / **than does John** ✓
